(Senderinfo).
Professor T

Professor Tempest (Ben Miller) ist wieder auf freiem Fuß und brennt darauf, sowohl an der Universität als auch bei den Ermittlungen mit seinen Polizeikollegen wieder aktiv zu werden. Doch seine Rückkehr wird von einigen Rückschlägen überschattet. An der Universität erwartet ihn die Nachricht, dass Haiden, der ihn während seiner Abwesenheit vertreten hat, weiterhin im Amt bleiben soll.

Zu allem Überfluss erreicht ihn direkt ein brisanter Fall: Innerhalb von nur zwei Tagen sind in Cambridgeshire sechs Menschen an einer Ethylenglycol-Vergiftung gestorben. Die Opfer könnten kaum unterschiedlicher sein: Amara, war Mitglied einer Laufgruppe, der auch Maiya Goswami (Sunetra Sarker) angehört, die neue Vorgesetzte von Lisa (Emma Naomi) und Dan (Barney White). Ein weiteres Opfer, Hal Harwood, betrieb mit seinem Bruder eine Schokoladenfabrik.

Während sich die Polizei bemüht, die Zusammenhänge zwischen den Todesfällen zu entschlüsseln, wird schnell klar, dass sie Professor Ts scharfen Verstand dringend brauchen, um Licht in diese rätselhafte Serie von Verbrechen zu bringen.
Professor T

Der Dekan hat Himmel und Hölle in Bewegung gesetzt, damit Professor T (Ben Miller) seinen alten Posten wieder einnehmen kann. Haiden soll dafür in Oxford einen neuen Job bekommen. \n\nDoch wenig später macht Haidens Frau Gisele (Robin Weaver) eine schockierende Entdeckung: Ihr Mann liegt tot in seiner Suite – erschlagen mit einer Champagnerflasche. Seine Uhr ist um 21:25 Uhr stehen geblieben, nur wenige Stunden nach dem Besuch eines Callgirls.
Professor T

Im Staffelfinale bekommt es Professor T. (Ben Miller) mit einem Autounfall zu tun. Eine Frau liegt tot am Unfallort, doch sie starb nicht als Folge des Unfalls. Während der Ermittlungen entdeckt der Professor verstörende Parallelen zu seinem eigenen Leben. Wie weit würde eine Mutter gehen, um ihr Kind zu schützen?\n\nWährend Adelaide (Frances de la Tour) nach einem schweren Sturz im Krankenhaus liegt, ist sie endlich bereit, ihrem Sohn die Wahrheit zu offenbaren. Doch die Lage spitzt sich zu: Lisa (Emma Naomi) setzt alles daran, den Mörder zu stellen, während Professor T. verzweifelt versucht, sie aufzuhalten.
Professor T

Wenn andere im Chaos versinken, beginnt für Professor Jasper Tempest (Ben Miller) erst die eigentliche Arbeit. Doch diesmal fordert der Fall auch ihn persönlich heraus. Auf einer Kreuzfahrt gilt eine Frau namens Ophelia plötzlich als tot. Tempest zweifelt – und liegt richtig: Sie war nie an Bord. Seine Schlussfolgerung führt zu einer gefährlichen Wahrheit, die ihren Ursprung bei Verlobtem JC hat. Als Jasper Ophelia aufspürt und befreit, eskaliert die Situation dramatisch und endet in einer bewaffneten Bedrohung.\n\nAbseits des Falls muss Tempest seine Routinen neu ordnen: Während seine Mutter unterwegs ist, übernimmt Tante Zelda die Aufsicht über Hund Kafka – ein kleines Detail, das den Professor mindestens ebenso aus dem Takt bringt wie der Kriminalfall selbst.
Professor T

Zelda hat ein Treffen mit dem Vater von Tempests Sekretärin. Denn zwischen den beiden hatte sich in letzter Zeit eine enge Freundschaft aufgebaut. Dieser lebt in einer Seniorenresidenz, in der ein Mord verübt wurde. Kurzerhand übernimmt Tempest (Ben Miller) den Fall. \n\nDoch Dan, der sehr um Lisa trauert, ist die Zusammenarbeit mit ihm zuwider. Trotzdem sind er und seine neue Kollegin Chloe, auf den scharfen Verstand von Tempest zur Lösung des Falls angewiesen.
Father Brown

Alec, der ungeliebte Bruder von Roger, erscheint auf einem Bowls-Turnier und wird erdrosselt. Er entpuppt sich als Polizist einer Sonderabteilung von Scotland Yard, die ehemalige Nazis aufspürt. (Senderinfo).
Father Brown

Am Schlosse von Lady Rose findet ein Tanz-Wettstreit statt, zu deren Teilnahme sich Bunty überreden lässt, als sie den blinden Alexander erblickt. Während des Tanzens stürzt Alexander und geht ins Treppenhaus, wo er im oberen Stockwerk Schritte hört. Als er nach oben geht, findet er Lucy in ihrem Zimmer ermordet vor... (Senderinfo).
Father Brown

Als Sheila und Philip, beide stellvertretenden Direktoren einer Jungen- bzw. Mädchenschule, einen Heizungsraum betreten, finden sie eine Schülerin schwer verletzt vor. Pater Brown vermutet mehr als nur einen Unfall und behält Recht, als sich herausstellt, dass May, die bewusstlos im Krankenhaus liegt, schwanger ist... (Senderinfo).
Father Brown

Der Amerikaner Reeve eröffnet mit einem Turnier seinen neuen Golfclub. Beim Ladies Cup entscheidet sich der Sieg zwischen Morgana, der Enkeltochter von Reeve, und einer französischen Dame, die sich als Bunty entpuppt. Als Bunty einen Ball aus einem Wasserhindernis schlagen muss, findet sie eine männliche Leiche... (Senderinfo).
Father Brown

Auf der Beerdigung von Flambeau taucht Lisandra auf, die Pater Brown bittet, ihr einen von Flambeau geschickten Schlüssel auszuhändigen. Doch im Pfarramt wurde eingebrochen und der Schlüssel gestohlen. (Senderinfo).
Moving On

Gerade erst haben sich die alten Unifreundinnen Claire und Evelyn nach vielen Jahren bei der Beerdigung ihrer Freundin Joyce wiedergetroffen, da offenbart Claire: „Ich werde den Bastard umbringen!“ Die Rede ist von Howard, dem Ehemann der verstorbenen Joyce. Vor vielen Jahrzehnten hat er Claire etwas Schreckliches angetan, für das sie sich nun rächen will.

Evelyn will ihre Freundin erst von der Idee abhalten, doch dann erlebt sie Howards Hass hautnah und erinnert sich daran, dass Joyce ihn einst als „grausam“ beschrieben hatte. 
Gemeinsam planen die beiden Frauen, den Tyrann ein für alle Mal aus dem Weg zu schaffen. 

Doch es ist gar nicht so leicht, sich eine Pistole zu beschaffen und den trauernden Witwer allein zu erwischen. Denn dummerweise hat Claire ihm gesagt, dass sie plant, ihn dieses Wochenende zu töten… 

Regisseur und Drehbuchautor Paul Weitz hat in seiner Karriere sowohl pubertäre Komödien („American Pie“) als auch Dramen („About a Boy“, „Fatherhood“) geschaffen. Mit „Moving On“ verbindet er beide Genres und schafft eine Geschichte, die sowohl humorvoll-abstrus als auch ernüchternd und berührend ist. Inmitten dessen brillieren Jane Fonda als nur auf den ersten Blick gefasste Dame und Lily Tomlin als ihre eigensinnige, nie um ein Wort verlegene Freundin. Starkes Schauspielerinnenkino!
Julie & Julia

Sie hat Entspannung dringend nötig: Julie Powell (Amy Adams) ist eine der Callcenter-Mitarbeiterinnen, die sich kurz nach 9/11 um die Angehörigen der Opfer kümmern. Nach Feierabend schmiedet sie die Idee, innerhalb eines Jahres alle 524 Gerichte aus Julia Childs Kochbuchklassiker „Mastering the Art of French Cooking“ zuzubereiten. Ihre Pfannenpannen und Psychocrashs will sie in einem Blog dokumentieren. 

Nebenbei erfahren Julie und wir, wie Julia Child (Meryl Streep) gut fünfzig Jahre zuvor zur Küchengöttin avancierte: 1949 kommt sie mit ihrem Mann, US-Botschafter Paul (Stanley Tucci) nach Paris, wo sie ein Faible für gute Küche entwickelt. Als einzige Frau mischt sich die resolut-exzentrische Lady unter die angehenden Profis einer Pariser Elite-Kochschule… 

Nora Ephron verstarb 2012 mit 71 Jahren. Der letzte Film der erfolgreichen Autorin („Harry und Sally“) und Regisseurin („e-m@il für Dich“) ist einer ihrer schönsten. Ausgehend von Childs Memoiren und Powells Bestseller „Julie & Julia“ verwebt sie mit leichter Hand und viel Esprit zwei Frauenbiografien aus unterschiedlichen Zeiten. 

Adams („American Hustle“) spielt Hobbyköchin Julie liebenswert, der Film gehört allerdings Streep: Wie sie mit Verve die überkandidelte Childs porträtiert, ohne sie zu veralbern, ist eine filmische Delikatesse. Dafür wurden ihr zu Recht ein Golden Globe und eine Oscar-Nominierung serviert.

Auf einem Weihnachtsmarkt bekommt die kleine Hannah (Imogen Tear) einen Strumpf geschenkt, in dem sie und ihre Mutter (Bridget Regan) immer wieder hilfreiche Dinge finden… \n\nGeht das Thema Trauerbewältigung für einen Hallmark-Film durchaus feinfühlig und fundiert an.

Norwegen im Jahr 1940. Kronprinzessin Märtha (Sofia Helin, „Die Brücke“) fürchtet nach dem Überfall Nazideutschlands auf Polen Schlimmstes. Mit Familie tritt sie vor der Besetzung die Flucht in die USA an. 

Unterschlupf findet sie im Weißen Haus, wo sie bald eine enge Freundschaft mit Roosevelt verbindet, gespielt von „Twin Peaks“-Veteran Kyle MacLachlan. Ihre Versuche, den Präsidenten von seiner Neutralitätspolitik abzubringen, gefallen längst nicht jedem… 

Emmy-gekrönte Miniserie.
Atlantic Crossing

Märtha wird von ihrem Onkel, dem schwedischen König Gustav, der mit den Nazis sympathisiert, unter Druck gesetzt. Er appelliert an Hitler und versucht, die norwegische Dynastie zu retten, indem er den kleinen Harald, jüngstes Kind von Märtha und Olav, zum König erklärt. Als Olav nach London flieht, liegt es an Märtha zu entscheiden, wie sie die Kinder in Sicherheit bringen kann. Mit ihrer Entscheidung akzeptiert sie, dass die Kinder ihren Vater vielleicht nie wiedersehen. (Senderinfo).
Atlantic Crossing

Die Atlantiküberquerung verläuft dramatisch. Als Märtha in den USA eintrifft, lädt Präsident Roosevelt sie als seinen Gast ins Weiße Haus ein und überhäuft sie und ihre Kinder mit Aufmerksamkeit. Die Stimmung kippt, als deutsche Bomben über London abgeworfen werden. Märtha fürchtet um Olavs Leben und erhält schlechte Nachrichten. (Senderinfo).
Atlantic Crossing

Nach dem Überfall Deutschlands auf Polen wächst die Kriegsgefahr auch in Norwegen. Obgleich Kronprinz Olav das Schlimmste fürchtet, versuchen er und seine Frau Märtha ihren drei Kindern Normalität zu vermitteln. Im April 1940 dringen die deutschen Truppen in norwegisches Territorium ein. Kronprinz Olav will als Offizier seine Pflicht erfüllen, ebenso sein Vater, König Haakon VII. Märtha und die Kinder flüchten. (Senderinfo).
Atlantic Crossing

Als die von Roosevelt angekündigte Militärhilfe, die er Norwegen zugesagt hat, nicht erfolgt, wählt Märtha den Weg in die Öffentlichkeit, um das amerikanische Volk um Hilfe zu bitten. Doch gerade als sie erste Erfolge erzielt, trifft sie ein unerwarteter Rückschlag. Offensichtlich für jedermann, erweisen sich die Gefühle des Präsidenten ihr gegenüber als tiefer, als es die Freundschaft erlaubt. (Senderinfo).
Atlantic Crossing

Die Japaner bombardieren Pearl Harbor. Der erschütterte Präsident bittet Märtha um ihre Zuneigung. Olav konfrontiert Märtha mit den Gerüchten über eine Affäre zwischen ihr und Roosevelt. Doch als unerwartete Bedrohungen auftauchen, brauchen sie und die Kinder den Schutz des Präsidenten. (Senderinfo).
Atlantic Crossing

Olav beschuldigt Märtha, die Kinder in große Gefahr zu bringen, ohne dass sie etwas für Norwegen erreicht hätte. Er stellt ihr ein klares Ultimatum. Märtha wird in Verlegenheit gebracht, als Präsident Roosevelt ankündigt, dass er ihr und dem Land Norwegen ein bedeutendes Geschenk machen wird. Im gleichen Atemzug fordert er jedoch von ihr ein, sie möge ihre Gefühle ihm gegenüber offenbaren. (Senderinfo).
Atlantic Crossing

Märtha erleidet einen großen Verlust und muss sich entscheiden, ob sie mit Ende des Krieges in den USA bleibt oder gemeinsam mit den Kindern nach Norwegen zurückkehrt. Doch bevor sie ein neues Leben beginnen kann, gibt es eine letzte Schlacht, der sich Märtha stellen muss. Vielleicht ist es die größte Schlacht ihres Lebens. (Senderinfo).

Trixie wurde der komplizierte Fall eines Kranführers zugeteilt, der nach einem Arbeitsunfall querschnittsgelähmt ist. Er wurde aus dem Krankenhaus entlassen und ist wieder bei Frau und Kindern. Inzwischen halten Nancy und Schwester Frances einen Vortrag über Aufklärung an einer Grundschule, und Lucilles Teilnahme an einer unkomplizierten Geburt nimmt eine tragische Wendung. Shelagh beschließt, einen Wohltätigkeitsbasar zu organisieren, um Geld einzunehmen, damit kaputte Geräte auf einem Spielplatz repariert werden können. Als Schwester Julienne einen verdächtigen Gegenstand findet, bricht Chaos aus. (Senderinfo).

Es ist der Oktober 1967, der Neuanfänge bringt. Schwester Crane ist auf Reisen, das aufregendste Abenteuer ihres Lebens, und Trixie pflegt ihre Patentante in Portofino. Schwester Hilda führt ein strenges Regiment, und Shelagh hat sich zum Team gesellt, um seine Arbeitslast zu erleichtern. Lucille bereitet sich auf ihren ersten Tag zurück am Arbeitsplatz vor, aber kommt damit offensichtlich nicht gut zurecht, trotz der Unterstützung durch das Team. Schwester Monica Joan ist erschreckt, als sie einen Raben im Wohnzimmer findet, weil sie seine Anwesenheit für ein Omen hält. (Senderinfo).

Ein unvorhergesehenes Ereignis in Poplar bedeutet, dass Haus Nonnatus so bedroht ist wie noch nie. Aber dieses Mal sind es nicht Ziegel und Mörtel, die in Gefahr sind – es sind die Menschen. Archie – Die Cary Grant Story

Ein Journalist sagte während eines Interviews einst zu ihm: „Jeder möchte sein wie Cary Grant.“ Darauf entgegnete der: „Ich auch.“ Cary Grant (1904–1986, gespielt von Jason Isaacs) wurde als Archibald Alec Leach im englischen Bristol geboren. Seine Kindheit ist schwierig, der Vater alkoholkrank, die Mutter psychisch labil. Als der Vater ihm mitteilt, dass seine Mutter gestorben ist und ihn daraufhin verlässt, geht es für Archie nach New York. Dort will er Ruhm und Reichtum erlangen. 

Die Kunstfigur Cary Grant wird zu seinem Schutz, 1962 ist er ein international gefeierter Star, doch hinter der strahlenden Fassade ist er einsam. Doch dann sieht der 58-jährige Cary die schöne 26-jährige Dyan Cannon in einer Fernsehshow und beginnt, sie zu umwerben. Sie ist sogar noch reizender, als er sie persönlich trifft. Er verliebt sich nochmal.

4 Folgen.
Archie – Die Cary Grant Story

Mitte Zwanzig hat Archie Leach damit zu kämpfen, sich in New York zu etablieren, als er durch eine zufällige Begegnung mit dem Komiker George zu einem Vorsprechen für ein Theaterstück kommt. Schließlich bricht Archie nach Hollywood auf, wo die Leinwandikone Mae West sein gutes Aussehen entdeckt und er sich einen neuen Namen aussuchen darf – Cary Grant. In den 1960er Jahren verliebt sich der erfolgreiche Filmstar Cary Grant mit Hilfe einiger Beziehungstipps von Grace Kelly in die junge Dyan Cannon. (Senderinfo).
Archie – Die Cary Grant Story

Cary (Jason Isaacs) gefährdet seine Beziehung zu Dyan, da er weder Kontrollsucht noch LSD-Konsum verbergen kann. Sie fühlt sich nach einem Auftritt in der Show von Danny Kaye nicht ausreichend wertgeschätzt: Trennung. Doch sie ist schwanger!

Archie – Die Cary Grant Story

Ein Journalist sagte während eines Interviews einst zu ihm: „Jeder möchte sein wie Cary Grant.“ Darauf entgegnete der: „Ich auch.“ Cary Grant (1904–1986, gespielt von Jason Isaacs) wurde als Archibald Alec Leach im englischen Bristol geboren. Seine Kindheit ist schwierig, der Vater alkoholkrank, die Mutter psychisch labil. Als der Vater ihm mitteilt, dass seine Mutter gestorben ist und ihn daraufhin verlässt, geht es für Archie nach New York. Dort will er Ruhm und Reichtum erlangen. 

Die Kunstfigur Cary Grant wird zu seinem Schutz, 1962 ist er ein international gefeierter Star, doch hinter der strahlenden Fassade ist er einsam. Doch dann sieht der 58-jährige Cary die schöne 26-jährige Dyan Cannon in einer Fernsehshow und beginnt, sie zu umwerben. Sie ist sogar noch reizender, als er sie persönlich trifft. Er verliebt sich nochmal.

Archie – Die Cary Grant Story

Mitte Zwanzig hat Archie Leach damit zu kämpfen, sich in New York zu etablieren, als er durch eine zufällige Begegnung mit dem Komiker George zu einem Vorsprechen für ein Theaterstück kommt. Schließlich bricht Archie nach Hollywood auf, wo die Leinwandikone Mae West sein gutes Aussehen entdeckt und er sich einen neuen Namen aussuchen darf – Cary Grant. In den 1960er Jahren verliebt sich der erfolgreiche Filmstar Cary Grant mit Hilfe einiger Beziehungstipps von Grace Kelly in die junge Dyan Cannon. (Senderinfo).

Moving On

Gerade erst haben sich die alten Unifreundinnen Claire und Evelyn nach vielen Jahren bei der Beerdigung ihrer Freundin Joyce wiedergetroffen, da offenbart Claire: „Ich werde den Bastard umbringen!“ Die Rede ist von Howard, dem Ehemann der verstorbenen Joyce. Vor vielen Jahrzehnten hat er Claire etwas Schreckliches angetan, für das sie sich nun rächen will.

Evelyn will ihre Freundin erst von der Idee abhalten, doch dann erlebt sie Howards Hass hautnah und erinnert sich daran, dass Joyce ihn einst als „grausam“ beschrieben hatte. 
Gemeinsam planen die beiden Frauen, den Tyrann ein für alle Mal aus dem Weg zu schaffen. 

Doch es ist gar nicht so leicht, sich eine Pistole zu beschaffen und den trauernden Witwer allein zu erwischen. Denn dummerweise hat Claire ihm gesagt, dass sie plant, ihn dieses Wochenende zu töten… 

Regisseur und Drehbuchautor Paul Weitz hat in seiner Karriere sowohl pubertäre Komödien („American Pie“) als auch Dramen („About a Boy“, „Fatherhood“) geschaffen. Mit „Moving On“ verbindet er beide Genres und schafft eine Geschichte, die sowohl humorvoll-abstrus als auch ernüchternd und berührend ist. Inmitten dessen brillieren Jane Fonda als nur auf den ersten Blick gefasste Dame und Lily Tomlin als ihre eigensinnige, nie um ein Wort verlegene Freundin. Starkes Schauspielerinnenkino!

A Very British Scandal

Rache, Sex, Intrigen! Im Zentrum der Anthologieserie steht die Scheidung des Herzogs und der Herzogin von Argyll, die in den 1960er-Jahren für rauschende Schlagzeilen in der Klatschpresse sorgte. Margaret Campbell (Claire Foy, „The Crown“) trennt sich von ihrem Ehemann Ian (Paul Bettany). Der verdächtigt seine Frau der Untreue, leakt anzügliche Fotos von ihr an die Medien. Eine öffentliche Schlammschlacht beginnt. Doch die Herzogin kämpft erhobenen Hauptes.
A Very British Scandal

Margaret verdrängt die nagenden Zweifel an ihrer Ehe und setzt den Plan fort, ihren Anspruch auf Inveraray Castle zu sichern. Doch ein privates Foto hat das Potenzial, alles zu zerstören, was sie je erreicht hat. Die pikante Aufnahme, die außereheliche sexuelle Aktivitäten dokumentiert, wird einen der skandalösesten Scheidungsprozesse in der britischen Geschichte anfachen. (Senderinfo).
A Very British Scandal

Die Fronten sind verhärtet, als sich der Herzog und die Herzogin von Argyll in eine schmutzige Trennung begeben, die sich im grellen Licht einer gierigen Presse vollzieht. Während der skandalöseste Scheidungsprozess des Jahrhunderts über Margarets Leben und ihren Ruf hereinbricht, muss sie sich entscheiden, ob sie sich still und leise aus dem Staub machen oder dafür kämpfen will, dass ihre Seite der Geschichte gehört wird. (Senderinfo).

Zwischen all den blitzenden Fassaden und gepflegten Gärten ist der klapprige Van der obdachlosen Mary Shepherd ein Ärgernis. Nur Bühnenautor Alan Bennett hat ein Herz und gestattet Mary, ihr fahrendes Zuhause vorübergehend in seiner Einfahrt zu parken. Daraus werden 15 Jahre und eine Freundschaft. Die Grantlerin hat Maggie Smith einfach drauf. \n\nNur wenige können in einen Gesichtsausdruck so viel Trotz, Provokation und Schroffheit legen wie die zweifache Oscar-Preisträgerin, die auch dieser Independent-Perle ihren Stempel aufdrückt. Smith spielte die Figur bereits im Theaterstück von Alan Bennett, der die Geschichte tatsächlich erlebte. Gedreht wurde sozusagen am Originalschauplatz: in Bennetts Einfahrt.

bbctwo: The four chefs who have survived the intensity of the heats are back in the kitchen. Now they must prove to Marcus and Monica that they have the consistency, confidence and creativity to take on the next level of the competition. First up is the invention test, where the chefs must put pistachio centre stage and show Marcus and Monica what they can do with it. It's an ingredient that naturally lends itself to pastry and desserts, but used cleverly in a savoury dish, it could give one chef the edge. Will anyone dare to take it somewhere unexpected? But the chefs aren't finished yet. Their next test takes them out of the kitchen and into the company of three of the country's most influential food critics: William Sitwell, Jimi Famurewa and, taking her place alongside them for the first time, Ixta Belfrage, a recipe developer and cookbook author who spent five years working at the Ottolenghi Test Kitchen. The chefs must cook a two-course menu that showcases their food, ideas and technical ability, knowing that every element will be scrutinised by some of the toughest palates in the business. This is their chance to prove they can produce food that excites and surprises. However, impressing three professional critics is no easy feat, and their verdicts could have a major bearing on what happens next. Back in the kitchen, Marcus and Monica must weigh up everything they have seen and tasted before deciding which chefs have done enough to progress. With only three places in knockout week available, one mistake, an underwhelming plate or a missed opportunity could make all the difference. Who will earn their place in the next stage – and whose journey ends here? The pressure is mounting as the chefs edge closer to the coveted MasterChef: The Professionals title. (Senderinfo).

In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president – a former boxer and soldier – as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda. But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British – with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime. With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? (Senderinfo).
The Great House Revival – The Old Herdsman's Cottage.

Entrepreneur Aoibheann has found the ideal location to retreat from her busy life in Galway – a modest derelict cottage in the heart of the Burren. But Aoibheann's creativity and plans for the cottage know no bounds, and if she can't rein in some of her ideas, will this renovation ever progress? (Senderinfo).

Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – Tess, Stuart, Eileen, Mel and Dan – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize. (Senderinfo).

Paul and Bob travel to County Tyrone to fish at Baronscourt Estate, hoping to catch a pike of a lifetime. They have access to two beautiful and secluded loughs, set in over 130 acres of rolling countryside, and the private use of one rowing boat – what could possibly go wrong? Pike are wily fish, always hiding in the dark reeds and waiting to ambush their prey. Bob has a fail-safe method to try, but will the duo be able to outwit the elusive creatures? (Senderinfo).

Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity's future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation. (Senderinfo).

Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question. (Senderinfo).

Ross Kemp presents this quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Catherine, Lisa, Michelle and Helen – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

Sean Fletcher and Edith Bowman explore the Manchester Food and Drink Festival, meeting passionate producers of chilli sauce, Eritrean curries and Italian biscuits among the stalls. Onkar Singh Purewal discovers how it is possible to grow tea in the Vale of Glamorgan, while farmer Jim Smith gets stuck into some sticky sweets. The differences between dried, tinned, homemade and carton soup are revealed. (Senderinfo).

Michael's journey along the coast of Northumberland continues towards the Farne Islands, takes in the holy island of Lindisfarne, and finishes in England's northernmost town, Berwick-upon-Tweed. On the largest of the Farne Islands, Inner Farne, Michael pitches in to help rangers clear a toxic plant which is invading the island. It's so prolific that it's threatening the native plants upon which seabirds depend for nesting. From the mainland, Michael sets off on a two-mile pilgrimage along a single-track causeway, which twice a day is covered by the North Sea. His destination is the holy island of Lindisfarne. Michael discovers that the island was chosen in the seventh century by St Aidan as the site for a monastery. Northumbria's patron saint, St Cuthbert, later became bishop there. The vicar of the island today shows Michael a full-sized reproduction of the beautifully illuminated Lindisfarne Gospels, the originals of which are held in the British Museum. Back on the East Coast Main Line, Michael hugs the North Sea coast, crossing the River Tweed on Robert Stephenson's Royal Border Bridge to reach Britain's most northern town, Berwick-upon-Tweed. Struck by the variety of accents and dialects in the north east, Michael learns what distinguishes a Geordie from a Smoggie. Only two-and-a-half-miles from Scotland, Berwick-upon-Tweed has a turbulent past and an intriguing custom, dating back to the 15th century. Michael begs permission from the town's mayor to join horses and riders in a ceremony to mark the border between Scotland and England along a line agreed in 1438. (Senderinfo).

The South American coastline is one of the most populated regions of the Caribbean, yet just beyond the large cities lies untouched wilderness. And where the two meet, Liz discovers the unique relationships between people and nature – starting with her ancestral home, Trinidad, and it's world-renowned Carnival. (Senderinfo).

Michael Aspel and the team are at Montacute House in Somerset. Among the finds are a set of chairs that witnessed the battle of Trafalgar aboard one of Nelson's ships, and a valuable postcard collection which began life as an occasional hobby. Also, a vicar's wife confesses to a weakness for vintage underwear. (Senderinfo).

Flog It! comes from the Museum of Science and Industry in Manchester. The show is packed with items from around the world, including an Inuit carving, a French book of butterflies and a ship that sailed the China seas. The experts are Anita Manning and Micheal Baggott. Paul Martin chances upon a rare and beautiful art book that is hugely contested in the saleroom. (Senderinfo).

Every day this week, celebrity contestants Catherine Bohart, Chesney Hawkes, Rebecca Keatley and Jason Mohammad take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games skateboard? (Senderinfo).

Winter may be closing in, but Adam Frost has thrown on his warm coat and is sharing some practical jobs and seasonal inspiration to keep gardens thriving through the colder months. From planting shrubs and creating a striking winter container to laying a brick path, there's plenty to be getting on with in preparation for spring. In Hertfordshire, Ashley Edwards is given an exclusive tour of a stunning walled garden. Rachel de Thame reveals her secrets for growing spectacular dahlias, while Joe Swift discovers an extraordinary garden in Dorset bursting with beauty and inspiring plant combinations. There's also an allotment gardener in North Yorkshire carrying forward a love of horticulture that runs in the family, and a garden designer shows how structure and form can transform a garden even in the depths of winter. (Senderinfo).

Nach einem glorreichen Sieg über die Germanen fällt der römische Feldherr Maximus (Russell Crowe) einer Intrige zum Opfer: Commodus (Joaquin Phoenix), der machthungrige Sohn des Kaisers (Richard Harris), erdrosselt seinen Vater und setzt auch den Krieger auf die Todesliste. 

Maximus entkommt nur knapp der Exekution, verliert seine Familie und wird als Sklave an eine Gladiatorenschule verkauft. Der Wunsch nach Rache hält Maximus am Leben. Der Kämpfer avanciert zum Star unter den Gladiatoren, und schließlich kämpft er im römischen Kolosseum vor seinem Erzfeind Commodus…

An diesem blutigen, finsteren und mit fünf Oscars gekrönten Werk von Ridley Scott („Blade Runner“) ist alles kolossal: die Schlacht in den Wäldern Germaniens, die Kulissen des alten Roms und die Schauspielkunst der beiden Widersacher.

Die Bürger Roms leiden unter Hunger und werden immer unzufriedener. Doch General Cajus Martius Coriolanus (Ralph Fiennes) zeigt wenig Mitgefühl – er steht offen auf der Seite der Reichen und verachtet das einfache Volk. Seine Arroganz führt schließlich zu einem blutigen Aufstand.

Trotzdem steigt Coriolanus politisch auf, denn seine Erfolge als Feldherr gegen die feindlichen Volsker bringen ihm Ansehen. Doch die mächtigen Politiker Roms sehen ihn als Bedrohung. Sie nutzen seinen Stolz, um die Bürger gegen ihn aufzuhetzen. Am Ende wird Coriolanus aus der Stadt verbannt.

Verbittert sucht er ausgerechnet bei seinem Erzfeind, dem Volsker Tullus Aufidius (Gerard Butler), Zuflucht. Er schließt sich ihm an – mit einem gemeinsamen Ziel: Rom zu zerstören. Doch als seine Mutter Volumnia davon erfährt, fleht sie ihn an, den Angriff zu stoppen. Coriolanus steht vor einer unmöglichen Entscheidung: Soll er seiner Familie treu bleiben oder seine Ehre bei den Volskern wahren?

Shakespeares kraftvolle Sprache macht einen ganz besoffen vor Glück, einige Szenen sind großer Tragödienstoff (z.B. das Flehen der Mutter, toll gespielt von Vanessa Redgrave). Aber die Verlegung des Stücks in die Gegenwart (Drehort: Belgrad) knirscht, die aktuellen Bezüge bleiben meist Behauptung. Zudem überreißt Fiennes sein Spiel.

In the fourth leg, the teams enter a new frontier, Australia. The sixth largest country on the planet and home to eight distinct climate zones, it's a land of extreme contrasts. Language barriers may have evaporated, but in their place is a new challenge, the budget, as the country delivers all teams a financial reality check. The teams descend on the fourth checkpoint in the tightest race yet, with a foot race to the sign-in book. (Senderinfo).

After a hair-raising drive across the Conor Pass and a spot of seaside silliness hitting golf balls into the ocean, Bill bids farewell to Chris O'Dowd. In County Clare, Bill and Tom's attempt to sneak unnoticed into a hurling match goes awry, before an emotional reunion recalls an unforgettable act of kindness. Then, a chance invitation in Ballybunion leads to a freezing Atlantic challenge. (Senderinfo).

Mr Friendlyface is particularly tetchy this morning. He is packing for a skiing trip, but a dragon has pinched his golden fleece, and he urgently needs the heroes to quest it back – how else will he stay warm and cosy on the slopes? However, when the heroes accidentally agree to let his niece Trixie tag along with them, they fear that her clumsiness and lack of hero skills will ruin everything. (Senderinfo).
Grizzy and the Lemmings: World Tour.
Winx Club – The Magic Is Back
Blue Peter: Secret Santa Showdown, Greg James and Festive Crafts.

(Senderinfo).
Life in a Cottage Garden with Carol Klein.

Plantswoman Carol Klein shares with us a year in her garden at Glebe Cottage in north Devon. Carol has looked after her garden for over 30 years, each with its own rewards and delights, as well as problems and challenges. Follow Carol as her garden grows, flourishes, dies and is reborn. The first episode covers January and February. The frosts have not yet released their grip on the garden, and the devastation of a hard winter is scattered all around. There is much to do – cutting back, preparing the soil and planting garlic. The first green shoots of the year begin to appear as drifts of snowdrops carpet the woodland floor and hellebores reveal their ravishing colours. A local woodsman joins Carol to lay a native hedge. Slowly, the first signs of spring appear. (Senderinfo).

Nature is full of extraordinary surprises, and Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin are uncovering some of its more curious mysteries. Why do foxes' eyes shine in the dark? How did fish farts almost cause an international diplomatic incident? Does ivy really damage the trees it climbs? And how exactly do sea anemones deliver their sting? Together, they get to the bottom of these fascinating wildlife questions, with plenty of surprising discoveries along the way. (Senderinfo).

Classic Ealing comedy about a whisky-laden ship that runs aground off the coast of the Outer Hebrides during the Second World War. The local islanders have depleted their supply of the amber nectar and are overjoyed at the thought of stocking up again. But it is Sunday, and the teetotallers object to making free with the unexpected cargo. (Senderinfo).
Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden.

Marcus makes plans to expand the smallholding's herb patch. A trip to Gloucestershire to see the UK's largest herb collection shows that even someone as experienced as Marcus can still learn a lot about ingredients. Back at the smallholding, gardener Anatoli shows Marcus how to look after the bees and harvest the honey, and Marcus brings in some junior chefs to get inspired in the way the kitchen garden is inspiring him. Once the new herbs are in place, Marcus cooks up a herby feast for the people who have helped him along the way. (Senderinfo).

A beautiful building in Bath. Martin meets a couple who have bought a flat in a period, listed building, and luckily for them, they own the flat below too. In West Yorkshire, Martel meets two pals hoping to turn four flats into six! (Senderinfo).

Zweiter Weltkrieg: Per Zufall erfährt US-Soldat Kelly (Clint Eastwood), dass die Deutschen in einer Bank in Lothringen einen Goldschatz deponiert haben. Mit einem Haufen schräger Vögel (u. a. Telly Savalas, Harry Dean Stanton und Donald Sutherland) gibt er dem Kitzel des Verbotenen nach und bricht in geklauten Panzern ins Feindesland auf…\n\nDer satirische Mix aus „Das dreckige Dutzend“ (1967) und den Italowestern jener Jahre ist ein schräger Spaß mit tollen Thrillereffekten und großen Explosionen. Passend dazu veralbert der Soundtrack von Lalo Schifrin („Mission: Impossible“) den „Morricone“-Sound der Sergio-Leone-Western.
Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest news, analysis, reaction and interviews from the afternoon's biggest football matches. (Senderinfo).

Im September 1944 springen in den Niederlanden 35.000 alliierte Fallschirmjäger hinter den feindlichen Linien ab, um sechs Rheinbrücken zu besetzen. Doch im Zielgebiet liegen starke deutsche Panzerverbände. Das Unternehmen „Market Garden“ endet in einem Fiasko, bei dem 17.000 Soldaten sterben…\n\n„Gandhi“-Regisseur Attenborough († 2014) drehte mit Stars in Kompaniestärke: Sean Connery, Michael Caine, Anthony Hopkins, Hardy Krüger, Robert Redford und andere standen für das aufwändige Schlachtengemälde stramm.

A selection of U2's most memorable BBC appearances, including early songs such as their first Top 40 hit, Fire, on Top of the Pops in 1981; I Will Follow from a 1982 appearance on teen magazine show Something Else; and Two Hearts Beat as One from a rarely seen visit to The Kenny Everett Television Show in 1983. Other highlights include their 2011 set at Glastonbury – which featured classic tracks such as Sunday Bloody Sunday, Where the Streets Have No Name and Pride (In the Name of Love) – and a 2009 performance of Vertigo that wasn't just at the BBC, but on it, with the band singing from the roof of Broadcasting House. (Senderinfo).
U2: Live on the BBC at Tate Modern

Global titans U2 perform at the Tate Modern in London for a truly unique live collaboration of music and art. Fifty years since the Dublin band formed at secondary school, the legendary four-piece return with their 16th album, Carnaval de Luz. For one night, they perform songs from the record and classic favourites, including Pride (In the Name of Love), Beautiful Day and With or Without You, visually accompanied by 77 Million Paintings, an artwork by producer, artist and long-time friend and collaborator of the band Brian Eno. (Senderinfo).

Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr, aka U2, join Vernon Kay to choose ten songs from their lives as they release their new album, Carnaval De Luz, their first in nine years. Fifty years since the band formed as teenagers at Mount Temple Comprehensive School in Dublin in 1976, U2 are now recognised as one of the biggest bands in history earning their spot in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2005. They've won more Grammy Awards than any other band in history, picking up 22 awards, while their seven awards for Best International Act is a Brit Award record that they share with Prince and Michael Jackson. Alongside the critical acclaim, U2 are one of the biggest selling acts of all time with 175 million album sales to their name and their U2 360 tour became the highest-grossing tour of all time while pioneering a more immersive concert experience for fans. Bono and Adam Clayton both appeared on the Band Aid record, before a breakout performance for the group the following year at the Wembley leg of Live Aid. Later in their career they headlined Glastonbury's pyramid stage in 2011 and became the first act to perform at the iconic Las Vegas Sphere in 2023. Now the band are back with a brand-new album, Carnaval de Luz, their first album in three years, alongside a world tour in 2027 marking their first UK stadium shows in a decade. (Senderinfo).

Bill's exciting new life comes crashing down when he learns that his lodgers have given themselves nicknames but left him out. Hurt, Bill ramps up his eccentricities in the hope of providing the inspiration for a new moniker, only for his odd behaviour to confirm the students' suspicion that they're living with a weirdo. (Senderinfo).

The county of Yorkshire is the setting for Christine Walkden's balloon tour of Britain. At Scampston Hall we discover two superstar garden designers and meet young gardener Nathan, who is just starting out. At York Gate Garden, Christine catches up with an old friend and we discover the Yorkshireman who was the father of aviation. (Senderinfo).

Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry. (Senderinfo).

Dougie is at Loch Tay in Perthshire, where he gets an insight into the lives or our Iron Age ancestors and visits a reconstructed crannog at a prime lochside location. Arlene is in the Carse of Gowrie to find out how the community won the right to buy and restore a historic orchard. Rosie is searching for Scottish truffles on the Isle of Bute, Shahbaz is in the Cowal Peninsula to meet the couple rewilding their dairy farm, and Anne is in Angus, where she meets the chocolatier using locally grown berries in her confectionery. (Senderinfo).

Matt Tebbutt delves into the archives to bring an array of delicious recipes from some favourite Saturday Kitchen chefs. Alison Roman serves up her date and caramelised lemon pot roast chicken with a herb, garlic and pistachio salad. Owen Morgan brings along a taste of Spain, combining the flavours of mountain and sea for his chicken and seafood Spanish rice finished with a sherry and garlic aioli. Jamie Oliver takes to the hobs with an alternative to a traditional Christmas lunch: roasted venison loin wrapped in prosciutto, with a rustic celeriac mash finished with a chocolate and red wine sauce. Mandy Yin delivers big flavours with her Malaysian mussel and pineapple curry before Helen McGinn transforms gin, rum and vodka into three delicious homemade liqueurs. And Luke Evans tucks into either his food heaven, banh mi, or his food hell, braised oxtail. Meanwhile, Rick casts his net in the hope of landing a trout, while the Hairy Bikers are in Majorca to whip up a local classic. (Senderinfo).

The four chefs who have survived the intensity of the heats are back in the kitchen. Now they must prove to Marcus and Monica that they have the consistency, confidence and creativity to take on the next level of the competition. First up is the invention test, where the chefs must put pistachio centre stage and show Marcus and Monica what they can do with it. It's an ingredient that naturally lends itself to pastry and desserts, but used cleverly in a savoury dish, it could give one chef the edge. Will anyone dare to take it somewhere unexpected? But the chefs aren't finished yet. Their next test takes them out of the kitchen and into the company of three of the country's most influential food critics: William Sitwell, Jimi Famurewa and, taking her place alongside them for the first time, Ixta Belfrage, a recipe developer and cookbook author who spent five years working at the Ottolenghi Test Kitchen. The chefs must cook a two-course menu that showcases their food, ideas and technical ability, knowing that every element will be scrutinised by some of the toughest palates in the business. This is their chance to prove they can produce food that excites and surprises. However, impressing three professional critics is no easy feat, and their verdicts could have a major bearing on what happens next. Back in the kitchen, Marcus and Monica must weigh up everything they have seen and tasted before deciding which chefs have done enough to progress. With only three places in knockout week available, one mistake, an underwhelming plate or a missed opportunity could make all the difference. Who will earn their place in the next stage – and whose journey ends here? The pressure is mounting as the chefs edge closer to the coveted MasterChef: The Professionals title. (Senderinfo).

In August 1972, Idi Amin is 18 months into his dictatorship. Supporters hail the new president – a former boxer and soldier – as a saviour, and his rise to power is greeted with celebration and hope across Uganda. But beneath the apparent social harmony, resentment runs deep. Until 1962, Uganda had been a protectorate of the British – with the British very much at the top of the pile, Africans at the bottom and Asians in the middle. Despite ten years of independence, many Africans feel that they are denied opportunities to improve their position in society. Idi Amin decides to exploit their feelings and increase support for his regime. With one announcement from the president, the lives of 80,000 people in Uganda are changed forever. In a bid to cement his leadership, Idi Amin announces that all Ugandan Asians must leave the country within 90 days. Will they be able to flee on their British passports? (Senderinfo).
The Great House Revival – The Old Herdsman's Cottage.

Entrepreneur Aoibheann has found the ideal location to retreat from her busy life in Galway – a modest derelict cottage in the heart of the Burren. But Aoibheann's creativity and plans for the cottage know no bounds, and if she can't rein in some of her ideas, will this renovation ever progress? (Senderinfo).

Roman Kemp, assisted by Sarah Greene, hosts the quiz show where contestants race in moving podiums across the studio floor. Correct answers get the players moving, while wrong answers will stop them in their tracks. Five contestants – Tess, Stuart, Eileen, Mel and Dan – battle across a series of fast-paced qualifiers and head-to-head races where the aim of the game is simple – make it to the finish line before your rivals. The winner then races against the track itself in an attempt to win the £5,000 cash prize. (Senderinfo).

Paul and Bob travel to County Tyrone to fish at Baronscourt Estate, hoping to catch a pike of a lifetime. They have access to two beautiful and secluded loughs, set in over 130 acres of rolling countryside, and the private use of one rowing boat – what could possibly go wrong? Pike are wily fish, always hiding in the dark reeds and waiting to ambush their prey. Bob has a fail-safe method to try, but will the duo be able to outwit the elusive creatures? (Senderinfo).

Humanity's very survival depends on water. But global reserves are rapidly shrinking with no end in sight thanks to unmitigated climate change, population growth and poor resource management. Over two-thirds of the global population are faced with water stress, while millions have already been displaced by intense water scarcity which is now replacing oil as the most likely cause of global conflict. Hannah Fry learns about the different ways in which technology could help secure humanity's future water needs. She witnesses the effects of water scarcity in Kenya and learns about how technological solutions are currently being harnessed to reverse this dire situation. (Senderinfo).

Game show in which 24 players compete to score points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the Impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode, there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question. (Senderinfo).

Ross Kemp presents this quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Catherine, Lisa, Michelle and Helen – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money, step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash. (Senderinfo).

Sean Fletcher and Edith Bowman explore the Manchester Food and Drink Festival, meeting passionate producers of chilli sauce, Eritrean curries and Italian biscuits among the stalls. Onkar Singh Purewal discovers how it is possible to grow tea in the Vale of Glamorgan, while farmer Jim Smith gets stuck into some sticky sweets. The differences between dried, tinned, homemade and carton soup are revealed. (Senderinfo).

Michael's journey along the coast of Northumberland continues towards the Farne Islands, takes in the holy island of Lindisfarne, and finishes in England's northernmost town, Berwick-upon-Tweed. On the largest of the Farne Islands, Inner Farne, Michael pitches in to help rangers clear a toxic plant which is invading the island. It's so prolific that it's threatening the native plants upon which seabirds depend for nesting. From the mainland, Michael sets off on a two-mile pilgrimage along a single-track causeway, which twice a day is covered by the North Sea. His destination is the holy island of Lindisfarne. Michael discovers that the island was chosen in the seventh century by St Aidan as the site for a monastery. Northumbria's patron saint, St Cuthbert, later became bishop there. The vicar of the island today shows Michael a full-sized reproduction of the beautifully illuminated Lindisfarne Gospels, the originals of which are held in the British Museum. Back on the East Coast Main Line, Michael hugs the North Sea coast, crossing the River Tweed on Robert Stephenson's Royal Border Bridge to reach Britain's most northern town, Berwick-upon-Tweed. Struck by the variety of accents and dialects in the north east, Michael learns what distinguishes a Geordie from a Smoggie. Only two-and-a-half-miles from Scotland, Berwick-upon-Tweed has a turbulent past and an intriguing custom, dating back to the 15th century. Michael begs permission from the town's mayor to join horses and riders in a ceremony to mark the border between Scotland and England along a line agreed in 1438. (Senderinfo).

The South American coastline is one of the most populated regions of the Caribbean, yet just beyond the large cities lies untouched wilderness. And where the two meet, Liz discovers the unique relationships between people and nature – starting with her ancestral home, Trinidad, and it's world-renowned Carnival. (Senderinfo).

Michael Aspel and the team are at Montacute House in Somerset. Among the finds are a set of chairs that witnessed the battle of Trafalgar aboard one of Nelson's ships, and a valuable postcard collection which began life as an occasional hobby. Also, a vicar's wife confesses to a weakness for vintage underwear. (Senderinfo).

Flog It! comes from the Museum of Science and Industry in Manchester. The show is packed with items from around the world, including an Inuit carving, a French book of butterflies and a ship that sailed the China seas. The experts are Anita Manning and Micheal Baggott. Paul Martin chances upon a rare and beautiful art book that is hugely contested in the saleroom. (Senderinfo).

Every day this week, celebrity contestants Catherine Bohart, Chesney Hawkes, Rebecca Keatley and Jason Mohammad take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, Michael Sheen. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted by the House of Games skateboard? (Senderinfo).

Winter may be closing in, but Adam Frost has thrown on his warm coat and is sharing some practical jobs and seasonal inspiration to keep gardens thriving through the colder months. From planting shrubs and creating a striking winter container to laying a brick path, there's plenty to be getting on with in preparation for spring. In Hertfordshire, Ashley Edwards is given an exclusive tour of a stunning walled garden. Rachel de Thame reveals her secrets for growing spectacular dahlias, while Joe Swift discovers an extraordinary garden in Dorset bursting with beauty and inspiring plant combinations. There's also an allotment gardener in North Yorkshire carrying forward a love of horticulture that runs in the family, and a garden designer shows how structure and form can transform a garden even in the depths of winter. (Senderinfo).

Nach einem glorreichen Sieg über die Germanen fällt der römische Feldherr Maximus (Russell Crowe) einer Intrige zum Opfer: Commodus (Joaquin Phoenix), der machthungrige Sohn des Kaisers (Richard Harris), erdrosselt seinen Vater und setzt auch den Krieger auf die Todesliste. 

Maximus entkommt nur knapp der Exekution, verliert seine Familie und wird als Sklave an eine Gladiatorenschule verkauft. Der Wunsch nach Rache hält Maximus am Leben. Der Kämpfer avanciert zum Star unter den Gladiatoren, und schließlich kämpft er im römischen Kolosseum vor seinem Erzfeind Commodus…

An diesem blutigen, finsteren und mit fünf Oscars gekrönten Werk von Ridley Scott („Blade Runner“) ist alles kolossal: die Schlacht in den Wäldern Germaniens, die Kulissen des alten Roms und die Schauspielkunst der beiden Widersacher.

Die Bürger Roms leiden unter Hunger und werden immer unzufriedener. Doch General Cajus Martius Coriolanus (Ralph Fiennes) zeigt wenig Mitgefühl – er steht offen auf der Seite der Reichen und verachtet das einfache Volk. Seine Arroganz führt schließlich zu einem blutigen Aufstand.

Trotzdem steigt Coriolanus politisch auf, denn seine Erfolge als Feldherr gegen die feindlichen Volsker bringen ihm Ansehen. Doch die mächtigen Politiker Roms sehen ihn als Bedrohung. Sie nutzen seinen Stolz, um die Bürger gegen ihn aufzuhetzen. Am Ende wird Coriolanus aus der Stadt verbannt.

Verbittert sucht er ausgerechnet bei seinem Erzfeind, dem Volsker Tullus Aufidius (Gerard Butler), Zuflucht. Er schließt sich ihm an – mit einem gemeinsamen Ziel: Rom zu zerstören. Doch als seine Mutter Volumnia davon erfährt, fleht sie ihn an, den Angriff zu stoppen. Coriolanus steht vor einer unmöglichen Entscheidung: Soll er seiner Familie treu bleiben oder seine Ehre bei den Volskern wahren?

Shakespeares kraftvolle Sprache macht einen ganz besoffen vor Glück, einige Szenen sind großer Tragödienstoff (z.B. das Flehen der Mutter, toll gespielt von Vanessa Redgrave). Aber die Verlegung des Stücks in die Gegenwart (Drehort: Belgrad) knirscht, die aktuellen Bezüge bleiben meist Behauptung. Zudem überreißt Fiennes sein Spiel.

In the fourth leg, the teams enter a new frontier, Australia. The sixth largest country on the planet and home to eight distinct climate zones, it's a land of extreme contrasts. Language barriers may have evaporated, but in their place is a new challenge, the budget, as the country delivers all teams a financial reality check. The teams descend on the fourth checkpoint in the tightest race yet, with a foot race to the sign-in book. (Senderinfo).

After a hair-raising drive across the Conor Pass and a spot of seaside silliness hitting golf balls into the ocean, Bill bids farewell to Chris O'Dowd. In County Clare, Bill and Tom's attempt to sneak unnoticed into a hurling match goes awry, before an emotional reunion recalls an unforgettable act of kindness. Then, a chance invitation in Ballybunion leads to a freezing Atlantic challenge. (Senderinfo).

Mr Friendlyface is particularly tetchy this morning. He is packing for a skiing trip, but a dragon has pinched his golden fleece, and he urgently needs the heroes to quest it back – how else will he stay warm and cosy on the slopes? However, when the heroes accidentally agree to let his niece Trixie tag along with them, they fear that her clumsiness and lack of hero skills will ruin everything. (Senderinfo).
Grizzy and the Lemmings: World Tour.
Winx Club – The Magic Is Back
Blue Peter: Secret Santa Showdown, Greg James and Festive Crafts.

Winter may be closing in, but Adam Frost has thrown on his warm coat and is sharing some practical jobs and seasonal inspiration to keep gardens thriving through the colder months. From planting shrubs and creating a striking winter container to laying a brick path, there's plenty to be getting on with in preparation for spring. There's also an allotment gardener in North Yorkshire carrying forward a love of horticulture that runs in the family, and a garden designer shows how structure and form can transform a garden even in the depths of winter. (Senderinfo).
Life in a Cottage Garden with Carol Klein.

Plantswoman Carol Klein shares with us a year in her garden at Glebe Cottage in north Devon. Carol has looked after her garden for over 30 years, each with its own rewards and delights, as well as problems and challenges. Follow Carol as her garden grows, flourishes, dies and is reborn. The first episode covers January and February. The frosts have not yet released their grip on the garden, and the devastation of a hard winter is scattered all around. There is much to do – cutting back, preparing the soil and planting garlic. The first green shoots of the year begin to appear as drifts of snowdrops carpet the woodland floor and hellebores reveal their ravishing colours. A local woodsman joins Carol to lay a native hedge. Slowly, the first signs of spring appear. (Senderinfo).

Nature is full of extraordinary surprises, and Chris Packham, Kyle Thomas and Megan McCubbin are uncovering some of its more curious mysteries. Why do foxes' eyes shine in the dark? How did fish farts almost cause an international diplomatic incident? Does ivy really damage the trees it climbs? And how exactly do sea anemones deliver their sting? Together, they get to the bottom of these fascinating wildlife questions, with plenty of surprising discoveries along the way. (Senderinfo).

Classic Ealing comedy about a whisky-laden ship that runs aground off the coast of the Outer Hebrides during the Second World War. The local islanders have depleted their supply of the amber nectar and are overjoyed at the thought of stocking up again. But it is Sunday, and the teetotallers object to making free with the unexpected cargo. (Senderinfo).
Marcus Wareing's Tales from a Kitchen Garden.

Marcus makes plans to expand the smallholding's herb patch. A trip to Gloucestershire to see the UK's largest herb collection shows that even someone as experienced as Marcus can still learn a lot about ingredients. Back at the smallholding, gardener Anatoli shows Marcus how to look after the bees and harvest the honey, and Marcus brings in some junior chefs to get inspired in the way the kitchen garden is inspiring him. Once the new herbs are in place, Marcus cooks up a herby feast for the people who have helped him along the way. (Senderinfo).

A beautiful building in Bath. Martin meets a couple who have bought a flat in a period, listed building, and luckily for them, they own the flat below too. In West Yorkshire, Martel meets two pals hoping to turn four flats into six! (Senderinfo).

Zweiter Weltkrieg: Per Zufall erfährt US-Soldat Kelly (Clint Eastwood), dass die Deutschen in einer Bank in Lothringen einen Goldschatz deponiert haben. Mit einem Haufen schräger Vögel (u. a. Telly Savalas, Harry Dean Stanton und Donald Sutherland) gibt er dem Kitzel des Verbotenen nach und bricht in geklauten Panzern ins Feindesland auf…\n\nDer satirische Mix aus „Das dreckige Dutzend“ (1967) und den Italowestern jener Jahre ist ein schräger Spaß mit tollen Thrillereffekten und großen Explosionen. Passend dazu veralbert der Soundtrack von Lalo Schifrin („Mission: Impossible“) den „Morricone“-Sound der Sergio-Leone-Western.
Jason Mohammad and guests bring you all the goals, latest news, analysis, reaction and interviews from the afternoon's biggest football matches. (Senderinfo).

Im September 1944 springen in den Niederlanden 35.000 alliierte Fallschirmjäger hinter den feindlichen Linien ab, um sechs Rheinbrücken zu besetzen. Doch im Zielgebiet liegen starke deutsche Panzerverbände. Das Unternehmen „Market Garden“ endet in einem Fiasko, bei dem 17.000 Soldaten sterben…\n\n„Gandhi“-Regisseur Attenborough († 2014) drehte mit Stars in Kompaniestärke: Sean Connery, Michael Caine, Anthony Hopkins, Hardy Krüger, Robert Redford und andere standen für das aufwändige Schlachtengemälde stramm.

A selection of U2's most memorable BBC appearances, including early songs such as their first Top 40 hit, Fire, on Top of the Pops in 1981; I Will Follow from a 1982 appearance on teen magazine show Something Else; and Two Hearts Beat as One from a rarely seen visit to The Kenny Everett Television Show in 1983. Other highlights include their 2011 set at Glastonbury – which featured classic tracks such as Sunday Bloody Sunday, Where the Streets Have No Name and Pride (In the Name of Love) – and a 2009 performance of Vertigo that wasn't just at the BBC, but on it, with the band singing from the roof of Broadcasting House. (Senderinfo).
U2: Live on the BBC at Tate Modern

Global titans U2 perform at the Tate Modern in London for a truly unique live collaboration of music and art. Fifty years since the Dublin band formed at secondary school, the legendary four-piece return with their 16th album, Carnaval de Luz. For one night, they perform songs from the record and classic favourites, including Pride (In the Name of Love), Beautiful Day and With or Without You, visually accompanied by 77 Million Paintings, an artwork by producer, artist and long-time friend and collaborator of the band Brian Eno. (Senderinfo).

Bono, The Edge, Adam Clayton and Larry Mullen Jr, aka U2, join Vernon Kay to choose ten songs from their lives as they release their new album, Carnaval De Luz, their first in nine years. Fifty years since the band formed as teenagers at Mount Temple Comprehensive School in Dublin in 1976, U2 are now recognised as one of the biggest bands in history earning their spot in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2005. They've won more Grammy Awards than any other band in history, picking up 22 awards, while their seven awards for Best International Act is a Brit Award record that they share with Prince and Michael Jackson. Alongside the critical acclaim, U2 are one of the biggest selling acts of all time with 175 million album sales to their name and their U2 360 tour became the highest-grossing tour of all time while pioneering a more immersive concert experience for fans. Bono and Adam Clayton both appeared on the Band Aid record, before a breakout performance for the group the following year at the Wembley leg of Live Aid. Later in their career they headlined Glastonbury's pyramid stage in 2011 and became the first act to perform at the iconic Las Vegas Sphere in 2023. Now the band are back with a brand-new album, Carnaval de Luz, their first album in three years, alongside a world tour in 2027 marking their first UK stadium shows in a decade. (Senderinfo).

Bill's exciting new life comes crashing down when he learns that his lodgers have given themselves nicknames but left him out. Hurt, Bill ramps up his eccentricities in the hope of providing the inspiration for a new moniker, only for his odd behaviour to confirm the students' suspicion that they're living with a weirdo. (Senderinfo).

The county of Yorkshire is the setting for Christine Walkden's balloon tour of Britain. At Scampston Hall we discover two superstar garden designers and meet young gardener Nathan, who is just starting out. At York Gate Garden, Christine catches up with an old friend and we discover the Yorkshireman who was the father of aviation. (Senderinfo).

Charlotte Smith and Sean Fletcher are in the Ceiriog Valley in north Wales, meeting former clinical vet Claire Whittle, who took on an upland farm two years ago. Charlotte finds out why Claire made the leap into farming and what regenerative farming means to her, before helping with health and pregnancy checks on her cattle. Sean gets stuck into a cow pat to explore the hidden world of dung beetles and helps plant trees in a new agroforestry field. Meanwhile, Tom investigates changes that could be coming for the game bird shooting industry. (Senderinfo).

Dougie is at Loch Tay in Perthshire, where he gets an insight into the lives or our Iron Age ancestors and visits a reconstructed crannog at a prime lochside location. Arlene is in the Carse of Gowrie to find out how the community won the right to buy and restore a historic orchard. Rosie is searching for Scottish truffles on the Isle of Bute, Shahbaz is in the Cowal Peninsula to meet the couple rewilding their dairy farm, and Anne is in Angus, where she meets the chocolatier using locally grown berries in her confectionery. (Senderinfo).

Owen Morgan brings along a taste of Spain, combining the flavours of mountain and sea for his chicken and seafood Spanish rice finished with a sherry and garlic aioli. Jamie Oliver takes to the hobs with an alternative to a traditional Christmas lunch: roasted venison loin wrapped in prosciutto, with a rustic celeriac mash finished with a chocolate and red wine sauce. Mandy Yin delivers big flavours with her Malaysian mussel and pineapple curry before Helen McGinn transforms gin, rum and vodka into three delicious homemade liqueurs. And Luke Evans tucks into either his food heaven, banh mi, or his food hell, braised oxtail. Meanwhile, Rick casts his net in the hope of landing a trout, while the Hairy Bikers are in Majorca to whip up a local classic. (Senderinfo).

Bob Wallace (Bing Crosby) und Phil Davis (Danny Kaye), zwei erfolgreiche Entertainer, organisieren eine rauschende Revue, um ein Wintersporthotel in Vermont vor der Pleite zu bewahren… \n\nNach einer Operette von Irving Berlin. Höhepunkt: Bing Crosby intoniert seinen Evergreen „White Christmas“.

On 24 September 2025, the main road outside one of Bangkok's major hospitals collapsed. The giant sinkhole, the size of two tennis courts, snapped water pipes, ripped down power lines, and swallowed two vehicles. During the day, it continued to grow, threatening the foundations of the hospital and forcing close to a thousand staff and patients to evacuate the building. Ampan Vimonvattana, vice dean of Vajira Hospital, witnessed the collapse: "The earth swallowed everything... it pulled the road surface, the soil, anything on top. Even the electrical poles got dragged down. It was really scary." Why Sinkholes Collapse explores cases of sinkholes in Godstone, Surrey, a collapse under a main road in Yashio City in Japan and the underground quarries that are beneath ten per cent of Paris to help explain why sinkholes occur and how they can be prevented. (Senderinfo).
Lucy Worsley's Keys to the Castle

Lucy Worsley travels to Venice, where she is given the keys to the Doge's Palace, a multi-purpose building that controlled Venice's empire for a thousand years. She has a close shave in the dreaded Council of Ten's torture chamber, discovers a 24-carat gold staircase that leads to one of the biggest rooms in Europe, and encounters hidden doors and secret messages. (Senderinfo).
New: Mortimer and Whitehouse: Gone Fishing.

Paul and Bob are in Hampshire to fish both the River Beaulieu and the adjoining Solent. They're here to catch mullet and later take a boat trip up the Solent to try for a smooth hound. The Beaulieu is one of only a handful of rivers privately owned in the UK. It's been property of the Montagu family since the 18th century, and Paul and Bob have been given special permission to fish here. Later, they are joined by their doctor friend Anand Patel for an evening tipple and an update on their health. Paul is keen to discuss his most recent diagnosis, while Bob asks Anand to examine his feet for a common sign of ageing. (Senderinfo).

As their adventure nears its end, Bill still finds time to terrify Tom with his driving. A stormy round with NFL star Jason Kelce brings refuge in a stone shelter on the 7th, complete with pints and sausage rolls. In Dublin, Bill puts Tom in the spotlight for a change, before the pair reach the Giant's Causeway and reflect on a journey that became about far more than golf. (Senderinfo).

6. Juni 1944. D-Day. Blutjunge, vor Angst kotzende US-Soldaten landen in  der Normandie, Kampfabschnitt Omaha - ein Inferno. Die GIs sterben wie die Fliegen. Hier gibt es keine Deckung vorm deutschen Feuer, keine Ordnung, nur endloses Grauen, einen Strand, der sich rot färbt vom Blut. Bis Captain Miller (Tom Hanks) und die Überlebenden seiner Kompanie eine Bresche in den Verteidigungswall sprengen. Jetzt sind die anderen dran mit Sterben.

Ein paar Tage später. Miller soll mit einer Gruppe von sieben Männern den Soldaten James Ryan (Matt Damon) aufspüren. Ryan steckt irgendwo im Kriegschaos hinter den feindlichen Linien. Seine drei Brüder fielen in derselben Woche. Ein US-General will ein Exempel der Menschlichkeit statuieren und diesen einen Soldaten zurück zu seiner Mutter bringen…

Steven Spielberg hat hier versucht, den ultimativen Kriegsfilm zu erschaffen. An der ersten Episode über die alliierte Invasion zeigt sich die ganze Kraft dieses Regisseurs - realistischer und schockierender ist das Grauen des Krieges noch nicht gefilmt worden.

Später stellt Spielberg philosophische Fragen nach dem Sinn von Befehlen, von Heldenmut und ruinierten Seelen. Spielberg sagt, es lohnt sich, für die Freiheit zu sterben. Dazu braucht man sehr viel Mut nach seinen ersten Bildern.

Fiona Bruce presents an hour of debate from Clydebank, with politicians, commentators and members of the public. On the panel, from the Scottish government, the economy, tourism and transport secretary Stephen Flynn; for Labour, the Scotland office minister Melanie Ward; the leader of the Scottish Conservatives Russell Findlay; the leader of Reform in Scotland Malcolm Offord; and Holly Bruce from the Scottish Greens. Watch or listen first on the BBC News Channel, iPlayer and Sounds at 9pm, or on BBC1 at 10.40pm. (Senderinfo).

When an old friend returns, Martha faces the danger of exposure, forcing her to confess all to Kurt and make a risky decision to trust him. They must both keep Kamilla onside, even whilst keeping secrets from her and one another. Fuelled by both his complicated entanglements with Martha and Kurt and an effort to outmanoeuvre her, Friedrich makes a drastic move to catch Martha out. (Senderinfo).

İki gurme yazar Mehmet Yaşin ve Teoman Hünal'la geziyoruz, yiyoruz, görüyoruz, öğreniyoruz. "Görevimiz Yemek" iki ustanın samimi, çekişmeli, eğlenceli sohbetiyle iştahınızı açacak. Türkiye'nin birçok yerinde göreceğimiz bu iki üstat gittikleri yerlerde yediklerini, içtiklerini kendi tarzlarına göre yorumluyorlar ve zaman zaman ayrı fikirlere düşüp birbirleriyle karşı karşıya geliyorlar. İki farklı tarzı barındıran ve her ikisi de alanının birer dehası olan Yaşin ve Hünal yemek için bulundukları mekanlarda, eğlenceli atışmalı sohbetin ortasına atıveriyorlar bizi. Ortam bazen kızışacak bazen samimi bir hal alacak bazen de eğlenceden dört köşe olacak. Bazen modern bazen otantik bir hale bürünecek olan program "Görevimiz Yemek" iki eski dostun birbirleriyle olan samimiyetinden doğan zevkli sataşmalarının olacağı bölümlerle ekranlarda olacak. DÜNYANIN EN ÖNEMLİ KÜLTÜR BAŞKENTLERİNDEN BİRİ OLARAK KABUL EDİLEN İSTANBUL. TARİHTEN SANATA, EDEBİYATTAN BİLİME, FARKLI ALANLARDA EŞSİZ KOLEKSİYONLARA VE DEĞERLERE EV SAHİPLİĞİ YAPAN MÜZELERİ İLE "İSTANBUL'UN MÜZELERİ" BELGESELİNDE EKRANA GELİYOR.
Kent belleğinde önemli yer tutan yapıların incelendiği ''Hafıza Durakları'' belgesel serisi, İstanbul'un tarihi mekanlarını tanıkların ve tarihçilerin gözünden ekrana getiriyor.
Ayhan Sicimoglu ile Limonata, izleyicilerini her ay dünyanin baska bir ülkesinde, farkli bir kültüre davet ediyor.

Farklı coğrafyaların tarihinden mimarisine, modadan yeme içme alışkanlıklarına kadar uzanan bir yolculuğa hazır mısınız? Deedra Aynaz Özlen kendine özgü eğlenceli anlatımıyla, gezip gördüğü yerlerin kültürel özelliklerini seyircilere aktarıyor.
Bu bölümde şehirdeki tarımsal dönüşümün en yaratıcı çözümlerinden biri olan terasta tarım konu alınıyor. Tarımı gökyüzüne taşıyan öncülerle buluşuyoruz.
Türkiye'nin ormanlari, ve farkli özellikleri Orman Mühendisi Prof. Dr. Erdogan Atmis ile kesfediliyor.
FERMAN AKGÜL, ŞAHMARAN'IN İZİNDE MARDİN'E GİDİYOR. BÖLÜMÜN KAPANIŞI İSE BELÇİM BİLGİN'İN SESLENDİRMESİYLE MASALIN ANİMASYONLU BİR ŞEKİLDE ANLATIMIYLA GERÇEKLEŞİYOR.
İlk bölümde, ülkemiz topraklarından geçerek Çin ile Avrupa'yı birbirine bağlayan, insanlık tarihinin en eski ve işlek ana yollarından biri olan İpek Yolu ekranlara geliyor.
Bu sezonda, Cumhuriyet ile kimliğine bürünmüş bizzat Mustafa Kemal Atatürk'ün eseri ve önderliğinde inşa edilen Ankara'nın bellek yapıları ekrana geliyor.
Sunuculuğunu Kubilay Tunçer'in üstlendiği Kalemimde Anadolu, Türk edebiyatının iz bırakan yazarlarını, onların metinlerinden yola çıkarak Anadolu'nun farklı coğrafyalarında takip ediyor.
Fatih Akın'ın bir filminden ilham alarak Almanya'dan Türkiye'ye göç eden macera tutkunu Franziska ile birlikte farklı seyahat tarzlarını deneyimleyerek dünyanın çeşitli rotalarını keşfe çıkıyoruz.
Türkiye'nin dört bir yanından, yaşadıkları şehre değer katan insanların hikâyelerini anlatan ''Şehre Umut Verenler'' küçük adımların büyük değişimlere nasıl öncülük ettiğini gözler önüne seriyor.
Farklı coğrafyalarda rengarenk kültürleri keşfe devam ediyor. Bu sezonda, doğası, sanatı, yemeği ve neşeli insanlarıyla latin kültürünü ekranlara taşıyor.
Az sonra İçinden Deniz Geçen Şehir S1 E başlayacaktır.
Sunuculuğunu Eylül Görmüş'ün üstlendiği seri, dünyanın farklı kentlerini, o şehirlerle özdeşleşmiş yazarların yaşamları ve eserleri üzerinden ele alıyor.
Deneyimli dalgiç Savas Karakas, suyun bizden gizlediklerinin izini derinliklerde bizler için sürüyor.

Vedat Ozan ve Piraye Yüksel'in konuk olduğu bu bölüm 1900'lerin başlarına başka bir gözle baktıracak.

Mimarlığın bir yaşam biçimi olduğunu ortaya koyan belgesel serisi ''Mimarların Evleri'' bu sezon, Avrupa'nın farklı şehirlerine uzanarak, çağdaş mimarların kendi yaşam alanlarını mercek altına alıyor.
Cenk ve Mike, Pisac'tan başladıkları Peru maceralarında, sıradışı bir rota ve sürpriz bir rehberle Machu Picchu'ya ulaşarak benzersiz bir keşif yapıyorlar.
Mert Gökalp ile Malezya'nın büyüleyici su altı dünyasına dalış yapıyoruz. Olağanüstü biyolojik çeşitlilik ve nadir rastlanan deniz canlıları, eşsiz bir görsel şölen eşliğinde ekranlarınıza geliyor.
Bu sezonda, Cumhuriyet ile kimliğine bürünmüş bizzat Mustafa Kemal Atatürk'ün eseri ve önderliğinde inşa edilen Ankara'nın bellek yapıları ekrana geliyor.

(DRAM,2006) HAPİSTEN SONRA NAMUSLU BİR HAYAT SÜRMEYE KARAR VEREN BİR HIRSIZ, TAMİRCİLİK YAPMAYA BAŞLAR... ALTAN ERKEKLİ VE GÜRGEN ÖZ'ÜN OYNADIĞI FİLMİN YÖNETMENİ MEHMET ULUKAN.
Papatya bir genç kızdır. Karabiber ise Papatya'nın babasının saz grubunda çalışır ve Papatya'ya sevdalıdır.
Ahmet Sesigürgil, kameranın ardındaki sanatı, bir sahnenin duygusunu ve kompozisyonunu nasıl belirlediğini anlatıyor.

Yetenekli müzisyen Hafız Yusuf Efendi, Pasa'nın konagına ders vermesi için davet edilir. Pasanın iki kızı da Yusuf'a asık olur.
Ilahi sanatçisi Abdullah Önül'ün sundugu programda çesitli ilahilere yer veriliyor.
